# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👆 👇 ✌ 👌 👌 ✌]

I'm the Deaf monkey. I can see the bomb: display shows 0, light is blue, and there are three wires — 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. I hear nothing, but I can see gestures. Mute has gestured to me: ✋ 👆 👇 ✌ 👌 👌 ✌ — seven symbols. I don't know what they mean yet; Mute has the manual and can read it, but cannot speak. Blind can touch the bomb but sees nothing. I need to figure out the wire-cutting rule from the manual, which only Mute knows.

My best move: describe what I see on the bomb so Mute (who has the manual) can match it to a rule, and so Blind knows the layout. Since Mute can hear my speech and see my gestures, and Blind can hear my speech but not gestures, I'll speak the bomb's exact state to both. I can't gesture anything meaningful yet since I don't know the manual's symbols. I'll just report the display, light, and wire colors in words — that's the most useful thing I can do right now.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb reads: display 0, light blue, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. I saw your gesture but don't know the symbols. Tell me the rule and which wire to cut.")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb reads: display 0, light blue, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. I can't touch it; you'll have to cut. Waiting on Mute for the rule.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👆 ✌ 🤟 🤟]

I'm Deaf. I still see: display 0, light blue, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Mute has now gestured a second string: ✋ 👆 ✌ 🤟 🤟 — five symbols, different from last turn. I can't read gestures as words; they're just symbols to me. Mute has the manual and can't speak, so gestures are Mute's only output to me, but I have no key for the gesture alphabet's meaning. Blind can't see gestures at all.

The critical problem: Mute can read the manual but can't speak, and gestures are opaque to me (I see symbols but they carry no defined meaning). Blind can hear speech but not gestures. So the only channel that carries *words* is speech — and only I (Deaf) and Blind can speak/hear. Mute can hear my speech but can only reply in gestures, which I can't decode and Blind can't perceive.

So I need Mute to convey the manual's rule in a way I can actually use. Since Mute can hear me, maybe Mute can gesture the *number* of the wire to cut in a self-evident way — but I have no agreed code. I should propose a code: I'll ask Mute to gesture a count (e.g., number of symbols = wire number), or better, I should establish a simple convention. Actually, the cleanest: ask Mute to gesture exactly one symbol per wire number, or point. But symbols are arbitrary.

Alternative: Blind can hear Mute? No — Blind cannot hear gestures, and Mute cannot speak. So Mute's only output is gestures, visible only to me (Deaf). So I am the sole receiver of Mute's manual knowledge. I must decode Mute's gestures.

Let me think about what Mute is doing. Mute knows I can't read the manual and can't decode arbitrary symbols. Mute is likely trying to communicate the wire number using a count or a recognizable pattern. The two strings: turn 1 had 7 symbols, turn 2 has 5 symbols. Maybe Mute is spelling out something, or maybe Mute is gesturing a rule.

I should respond by proposing a simple, unambiguous code and asking Mute to confirm. E.g., "gesture the number of the wire to cut as that many ✊ symbols" or "point to the wire number by gesturing 👆 repeated N times." Let me propose: gesture N fingers/symbols where N = wire number, using a fixed symbol. That's decodable by count alone.

I'll speak to Mute (Mute hears me) and to Blind (Blind hears me) explaining the plan, and propose the counting code.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I can't decode arbitrary symbols. Use a count: gesture the wire number as that many identical symbols, e.g. one symbol for wire 1, two for wire 2, three for wire 3. Confirm the rule and the wire.")
speak(to="blind", text="Still display 0, light blue, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Mute can only gesture to me; I'm trying to get the rule. Stand by to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆]

I'm Deaf. Bomb unchanged: display 0, light blue, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Mute has now gestured exactly three identical symbols: 👆 👆 👆. I proposed the counting code last turn — "gesture the wire number as that many identical symbols." Three identical symbols = wire 3, the red wire.

But I must be careful. Mute heard my proposal (Mute can hear me). Three 👆 could mean wire 3, or it could be a coincidence. It's a clean match to my proposed code, and Mute had no other agreed code. Also, the earlier strings (7 symbols, then 5 symbols) don't fit the count code for wires 1–3, so Mute seems to have switched to my convention. That's strong evidence.

However, I should double-check against the bomb state. The manual rule for a blue light with display 0 and these wire colors — I don't know it. I'm trusting Mute's decoded answer. But wait: could "three" mean something else, like "cut the third one from a different ordering"? My code said "wire number as that many symbols," so three = wire 3. Red.

Blind needs to actually cut. Blind can hear my speech. I must tell Blind clearly: cut wire 3 (red). I should also confirm to Mute that I read it as wire 3.

One risk: I'm the only one who can see the light/display, and I've reported them. Mute has the manual and presumably matched. I'll go with wire 3.

Let me send: to Blind, cut wire 3 (red). To Mute, confirm reading = wire 3.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 3, the red one. Mute signalled three identical symbols matching our count code = wire 3.")
speak(to="mute", text="Reading your three symbols as wire 3, red. Telling Blind to cut wire 3. Confirm if wrong.")
wait()
```
